Meeting header:

Transcript body:
[00:00] Alex: Hi everyone thanks for joining, uh this is Alex from Redwood Inference, i'm the AE on this account, we also have Maya our solutions engineer. how's everyone doing?
[00:06] Chris: Good thanks, sorry for the slight delay, had a last minute call. we're doing vendor risk assessment for new LLM infra, so wanted to run through the security questionnaire and what evidence you can provide.
[00:14] Alex: totally, that's the plan. quick agenda - high level compliance attestation we can provide, common evidence (SOC2, pen test, CAIQ/SIG), and then dig into RBAC, SSO, logs, encryption and data residency.
[00:23] Priya: quick thing on our side - Quantum Systems requires EU data residency for any PII and prefer customer-managed keys if possible. also procurement wants the CAIQ answered within two weeks.
[00:34] Maya: great, thanks Priya. to set expectations — for hosted customers we provide SOC2 Type II reports and pen test summaries and we can complete CAIQ items; for private deployments we can support VPC/on-prem with KMS integrations, customer-managed keys via bring-your-own-kms or HSM integrations.
[00:49] Jake: when you say BRING your own KMS, is that like AWS KMS only, or can we use Azure Key Vault?
[00:55] Maya: both, we integrate with AWS KMS, Azure Key Vault, and GCP Cloud KMS; we also have partners for HSM if you need FIPS-level HSM. sometimes the transcript generator writes it as "Redwood Dedication".. that was a funny one we saw in other calls.
[01:12] Chris: ha, noted. can you confirm encryption at rest and in transit? and which ciphers, we have audit requirements for TLS 1.3 and AES-GCM or better.
[01:20] Maya: yes encryption in transit is TLS 1.2+ and we recommend TLS 1.3, at rest we use envelope encryption with customer or provider KMS and AES-256 GCM as the block cipher. i'll annotate that in the CAIQ answers.
[01:31] Chris: perfect. next - audit logs: retention, access, and tamper evidence. we need immutable logs retained for 2 years and an export path for SOC evidence.
[01:40] Alex: we keep operational audit logs in the control plane for 13 months by default, but for Dedicated/Private we can arrange longer retention or ship logs to your SIEM (S3, GCS or syslog) and discuss WORM-like retention via your storage tier.
[01:55] Priya: 13 months default is ok but we need 2 years. how does that work for hosted?
[02:00] Maya: for hosted the standard offering is 13 months; we can do a contract addendum for extended retention for enterprise customers or we recommend Dedicated where you can control retention locally. i can include options in the follow-up doc.
[02:11] Chris: can you produce an integrity / tamper-evidence mechanism?
[02:14] Maya: yes, logs are signed and checksumed in transit to our immutable store and we provide log hashes for audit, we'll include that detail in the security pack.
[02:25] Jake: about certifications — you said SOC2 Type II, do you have ISO 27001?
[02:29] Alex: we are SOC2 Type II for our hosted control plane, and we have ISO 27001 in progress, not yet certified across all regions. we'll share the current scope doc and timeline.
[02:38] Chris: that's important to note for procurement, thanks. regarding RBAC and SSO — we need role separation, least privilege, and integration with our SAML IdP.
[02:47] Maya: our console supports SSO via SAML 2.0 and OIDC; you can provision via SCIM in Dedicated/Private; RBAC supports fine-grained roles at org, project, and model level. note: on older exports sometimes it shows as SCIM/SCM, transcript's a bit messy but we'll send canonical docs.
[03:05] Priya: SCIM provisioning - do you support user deprovisioning hooks? we need immediate deprovision on offboard.
[03:10] Maya: yes, SCIM support includes immediate deprovisioning and we support push and pull sync. for Hosted we recommend session durations and short lived tokens. for Dedicated you can map to your internal directory.
[03:21] Chris: about private deployment — if we go on-prem what is the minimal network footprint and what ports need to be opened?
[03:27] Maya: i'll put a minimal diagram in the follow-up — typically you need access for the control plane or an air-gapped control plane option, postgres/mysql for metadata if you host it, and gRPC or HTTP ports between inference pods; we'll provide an exact list.
[03:41] Alex: also want to call out model custody — customers can pin model versions, and for private you can control model artifacts in your storage. we'll include the model artifact handling section.
[03:52] Chris: pen tests — can you share redacted reports?
[03:55] Alex: yes, we can share a pen test summary and redacted report; full reports may require an NDA, we can work that out, we usually provide executive summary and remediation timeline.
[04:07] Priya: CAIQ — do you pre-fill answers? procurement wants a pre-filled CAIQ so we can review faster.
[04:12] Maya: yes we prefill CAIQ and SIG answers for common vendor questions and flag items that require architecture decisions. we'll attach a prefilled CAIQ with annotations.
[04:21] Jake: what's your policy on data residency and cross-border transfers?
[04:24] Alex: for hosted customers you can select region controls, we have regional deployments in EU and NA, and we don't replicate customer PII outside of selected region unless you opt in. for Dedicated/Private you control data residency fully.
[04:38] Chris: do you offer contract language for data processing addendum and SCCs?
[04:42] Alex: yes DPA and SCCs available, we have standard language and can accept custom clauses for enterprise contracts.
[04:49] Priya: audit rights — do you allow customers to run their own audits or to request evidence in a certain cadence?
[04:55] Maya: customers get audit logs, SOC2 reports, and we support customer audit rights for enterprise with defined scope and NDAs; remote audits can be arranged.
[05:07] Chris: one of our controls needs cryptographic key lifecycle documentation and attestations. can you provide KMS key rotation policies and support for rotate-on-demand?
[05:16] Maya: yes we support automatic rotation and manual rotate-on-demand for customer-managed keys where supported. we'll include rotation docs and SLAs in the security pack.
[05:27] Jake: do you have a list of sub-processors? procurement requires a sub-processor list and notification policy.
[05:33] Alex: yes we maintain a sub-processor list and notification cadence; we'll attach the current list to the package.
[05:39] Chris: anything about incident response and timelines? we need 24/7 incident contact and SLA for major incidents.
[05:44] Alex: our incident response is 24/7 via the enterprise on-call, we have an incident handling policy with 1 hour initial response for Sev 1 and post-incident reports. we'll include a redacted incident plan.
[05:54] Priya: excellent. procurement wants to see sample contract language on indemnity and liability cap tied to data residency — is that negotiable?
[06:01] Alex: yes that's typically negotiated on enterprise deals. we'll have legal follow-up.
[06:05] Chris: can you walk us through a couple of CAIQ questions live? for example, network security and encryption controls - how do you answer these?
[06:12] Maya: sure. CAIQ question: do you encrypt data at rest? answer: yes, envelope encryption, AES-256 GCM; CAIQ question: do you support customer-managed keys? answer: yes, AWS KMS, Azure Key Vault, GCP KMS, HSM available for private deployments. i'll type these into the CAIQ and flag any items that need a follow-up.
[06:34] (slight crosstalk)
[06:36] Priya: on logging we need evidence for privileged access reviews. do you provide periodic access review exports?
[06:42] Maya: yes exports and we can run quarterly privileged access review reports; for Dedicated you can run these internally and for Hosted we can provide the exports.
[06:50] Chris: about backup and restore for model artifacts - we need RTO/RPO targets.
[06:54] Maya: typical RTO is 4 hours for critical infra in Dedicated setups depending on architecture, RPO is configurable. we'll include backup architecture and RTO/RPO examples.
[07:06] Alex: wrapping some things up - i'll send the security-pack link with SOC2, pen test summary, CAIQ prefill and sub-processor list. maya will produce a deployment diagram and RBAC/SSO guide.
[07:18] Chris: sounds good, procurement wants CAIQ within two weeks.
[07:21] Jake: yep that's our timeline.
[07:23] Alex: next call - technical deep dive for private deployment week of May 4, is that still okay?
[07:27] Priya: yes that works.
[07:29] Maya: i'll schedule with infra owners.
[07:31] (background noise)
[07:35] Chris: one last question — for audit logs can you provide tamper-evidence chain, like signed hash values we can verify?
[07:41] Maya: yes we provide log signatures and periodic hash summaries, we'll include sample verification steps.
[07:46] Alex: ok great thanks all, we'll follow up with the package and next steps.
[07:51] Chris: thank you.
[07:53] Jake: thanks everyone.
